editorial:
Imagine being a quiet country girl suddenly thrown into a fancy city home where almost nobody wants you there. That is exactly what happens to young Iris. She moves from her cozy forest cottage to Helsinki to live with her uncle, a bank manager, so she can finally go to school. While her uncle is kind, his wife and older kids treat her like an outsider because she is poor. You will feel for Iris as she tries to fit in, but you will also love the sweet bond she forms with the youngest child and the family cook, who are the only ones showing her any real love.

What makes this story work is how it shows the struggle between kindness and greed. The acting feels very real, and you can really tell when the tension in the house reaches a boiling point. It is a slow-burn drama, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy heartfelt family stories, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality. It is a great choice for a cozy movie night with the family.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the uncle's money troubles get worse. The mean family members try to take advantage of Iris's inheritance to save themselves. However, the truth about the money and the family's greed comes out in the end. Iris finds the support she needs, and the people who were actually kind to her are rewarded. She finally finds a place where she truly belongs, proving that heart is more important than wealth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school family dramas and stories about underdogs.
